openings: This lease is made between {{first}} (the "Landlord") and {{second}} (the "Tenant").

The Landlord lets to the Tenant the whole of the second floor of Harcourt House, 14 Quayside Road, Bristol (the "Premises"), for a term of five years starting on 1 March 2027 (the "Term"). The Tenant may also use the entrance hall, lifts, stairs and toilets of the building in common with the Landlord's other tenants. The Premises are let as offices, on the terms of this lease.
{{first}} ("{{firstShort}}" or the "Landlord") grants this lease to {{second}} ("{{secondShort}}" or the "Tenant").

By this lease {{firstShort}} lets the office premises on the second floor of Harcourt House, 14 Quayside Road, Bristol (the "Premises") to {{secondShort}} for five years from 1 March 2027 (the "Term"), for use as offices. The Tenant may use the common parts of the building, including the entrance hall, lifts, stairs and toilets, in common with the Landlord's other tenants.

sections.heading: Rent
variants: The Tenant shall pay a yearly rent of £84,000, excluding VAT, by equal quarterly payments in advance on the usual quarter days, the first payment to be made on 1 March 2027 for the period up to the next quarter day.
If any rent is unpaid fourteen days after it falls due, the Tenant shall pay interest on it at four per cent above the Bank of England base rate until it is paid.
The rent is £84,000 a year plus VAT, payable quarterly in advance by bank transfer. The rent for the first three months of the Term is waived to allow the Tenant to fit out the Premises.
The rent will be reviewed on the third anniversary of the start of the Term to the open market rent at that date, but it will never go down on review.

sections.heading: Service Charge and Outgoings
variants: In addition to the rent, the Tenant shall pay, as a service charge, a fair proportion of the Landlord's costs of repairing, cleaning, lighting and insuring the building and its common parts. The Landlord shall send the Tenant an estimate before each year and a certified statement of actual costs after it.
The Tenant shall also pay all business rates and utility charges for the Premises.

The Tenant shall pay a service charge of twenty per cent of the Landlord's costs of running the building, including repairs to its structure and common parts, security, cleaning and the building's insurance, by quarterly payments on account with the rent, adjusted when the year's accounts are prepared. The Tenant pays its own business rates, electricity, water and telephone charges.

sections.heading: Use
variants: The Tenant shall use the Premises only as offices and for no other purpose. It shall not do anything at the Premises that causes a nuisance to the Landlord or to other occupiers of the building, or that may invalidate the building's insurance.

The Premises may be used only as offices within Class E of the Use Classes Order. The Tenant shall comply with the regulations the Landlord reasonably makes for all occupiers of the building, and shall not hold any auction, sale or public meeting at the Premises.

sections.heading: Repair and Alterations
variants: The Tenant shall keep the interior of the Premises in good repair and decorative condition, but need not put them in a better state than that shown in the schedule of condition the parties signed with this lease.
The Tenant shall make no structural alterations. It may install or move internal partitions with the Landlord's consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

The Tenant shall keep the inside of the Premises, including the floors, ceilings, internal walls, doors and windows, clean and in good repair, and shall redecorate them in the last year of the Term. The Landlord shall repair the structure and the common parts.
The Tenant may not alter the Premises without the Landlord's written consent, except for non-structural internal works that it notifies to the Landlord in advance.

sections.heading: Assignment and Underletting
variants: The Tenant shall not assign or underlet the whole of the Premises without the Landlord's consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, and shall not assign or underlet part only of them. The Tenant may share occupation with a company in its group, provided no tenancy is created.

The Tenant may assign this lease, or underlet the whole of the Premises, only with the Landlord's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed. On an assignment, the Landlord may require the outgoing Tenant to guarantee the incoming tenant's obligations by an authorised guarantee agreement.

sections.heading: Break Option
variants: The Tenant may end this lease on the third anniversary of the start of the Term by giving the Landlord at least six months' written notice, provided it has paid all rent due and gives up the Premises free of any occupiers on the break date.

The Tenant has one right to break this lease at the end of the third year of the Term. To use it, the Tenant must give the Landlord not less than six months' written notice and, on the break date, have paid the rent in full and vacated the Premises.

sections.heading: Landlord's Obligations and Forfeiture
variants: The Landlord shall insure the building against the usual risks and allow the Tenant quiet enjoyment of the Premises for the Term, so long as the Tenant pays the rent and observes this lease.
If the rent is unpaid for twenty-one days after it falls due, or the Tenant materially breaches this lease or becomes insolvent, the Landlord may re-enter the Premises and this lease shall end.

So long as the Tenant pays the rent and complies with this lease, it may occupy the Premises without interruption by the Landlord, who shall keep the building insured. The Landlord may end this lease by re-entering the Premises if any rent is twenty-one days overdue, if the Tenant breaks a covenant in this lease and does not remedy it, or if the Tenant becomes insolvent.

sections.heading: End of the Lease
variants: At the end of the Term, or on earlier termination, the Tenant shall give back the Premises in the repair and condition this lease requires, remove its furniture and signs, and make good any damage caused by removing them. The parties agree that the security of tenure provisions of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1954 do not apply to this lease.

When this lease ends, the Tenant shall vacate the Premises, return all keys and access cards, and remove any alterations the Landlord asks it to remove, making good the Premises afterwards. Before this lease was granted, the parties excluded the Tenant's right to a new lease under the Landlord and Tenant Act 1954.
